$comment: pd-vault known-answer vectors, v1 — copied byte-for-byte from the canonical Rust kernel crate core/kernel/pd-vault (branch claude/pd-vault-crate, PR #9313: src/kdf.rs and src/seal.rs test constants). Provenance, stated plainly (same words as the Rust source): the bytes came out of that implementation and were pasted back in; they are NOT RFC vectors. They were reproduced once during pd-vault development by a throwaway reference implementation written straight from RFC 8439 / draft-irtf-cfrg-xchacha, which is why they are believed correct rather than merely self-consistent. Per the ADR-0120 rule (no second implementation without a shared fixture), every non-Rust twin of the vault — the daemon's pure-TS reference seal in lib/pd-vault-ts.ts today, Workers or Swift later — asserts these exact vectors, so the implementations can only drift loudly.

derivation.kdf: channel_key = HKDF-SHA256(salt = channel_key_label, ikm = harbor_secret, info = unambiguous_encoding([channel_key_label, channel_id, u64_be(epoch)]), len = 32)
derivation.encoding: unambiguous_encoding(components) = u32_be(count) || for each component: u32_be(len) || bytes — prefix-free, no reserved separator byte
derivation.seal: XChaCha20-Poly1305(key = channel_key, nonce = 24 bytes, aad = unambiguous_encoding([seal_aad_label, harbor_id, channel_id, u64_be(epoch), u64_be(seq)])), ciphertext = body || 16-byte tag

encoding_layout.$comment: Byte-for-byte layout pin from pd-vault lib.rs test encoding_layout_is_stable: components ['hi', 0xff00] encode as count, then len||bytes per component.
